cards.text: Friend, Jesus is teaching in parables, everyday stories with a big truth tucked inside. He puts another one before the people listening. The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field.
Good seed, good field, good start. Then night comes and everyone is asleep, and you KNOW what that means: something's about to happen nobody signed up for.

cards.question: While everyone is asleep, who sneaks into the man's field?
Out in the man's field, the intruder sows ___ among the wheat.

cards.text: And then he slips away. Sowing weeds and sneaking off is the farm version of the coworker who jams the copier and quietly walks back to his desk like NOTHING happened.

cards.question: True or false: In the man's field, the weeds show up the very next morning, before the wheat even sprouts.

cards.text: Once the weeds appear, the owner's servants come to him. They ask, “Sir, didn’t you sow good seed in your field? Where then did the weeds come from?”

cards.question: How does the owner answer his servants when they ask where the weeds came from?

cards.text: The servants ask him, “Do you want us to go and pull them up?” I bet those servants already have their sleeves rolled up, friend. They are READY.

cards.question: True or false: The owner tells his servants to go pull up the weeds right away.
Why doesn't the owner want his servants pulling up the weeds now?

answers.text: They might uproot the wheat too
The weeds will die on their own
The servants need to rest first

cards.text: So the owner says, “Let both grow together until the harvest.” Friend, I waited YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, so this man has my full respect.

cards.question: At harvest time, the owner will have the harvesters collect the ___ first, then gather the ___ into his barn.
What does the owner say will happen to the weeds once they're tied in bundles?

answers.text: They will be sold at market

cards.text: Jesus puts another parable before them. The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man took and planted in his field.
Jesus says it is the smallest of all seeds. Friend, I drop ONE sprinkle on my bakery floor and it's gone FOREVER, so imagine planting something that small and expecting anything.

cards.question: In Jesus' parable, what does that tiny mustard seed grow into?
True or false: The mustard plant gets so big that the birds of the air come and nest in its branches.

cards.text: He told them still another parable, and this one has a woman working with three measures of flour. Flour? Now you're in MY department, friend. I'm a cookie man, but I know dough.

cards.question: Jesus says the kingdom of heaven is like ___ that a woman mixed into three measures of flour.
Once the woman mixes the leaven in, how much of the flour ends up leavened?

cards.text: Weeds, a seed, some leaven. BOOM, BOOM, BOOM, three parables back to back. Jesus spoke all these things to the crowds in parables.

cards.question: True or false: When Jesus teaches the crowds here, He tells them some things without using a parable.

cards.text: And this fulfilled what was spoken through the prophet: “I will open My mouth in parables.”

cards.question: In the prophet's words about opening his mouth in parables, what does he say he will utter?

answers.text: Things hidden since the world began
Songs sung in the days of old

cards.text: Then Jesus dismisses the crowds and goes into the house. His disciples come to Him with a request.

cards.question: Which parable do the disciples ask Jesus to explain?

cards.text: And Jesus explains it, piece by piece. Friend, I shared that junk drawer with a stack of old instruction manuals, and not ONE of them ever explained anything this clearly.

cards.question: In the parable of the weeds, who does Jesus say is the One who sows the good seed?
In Jesus' explanation, the field is the ___.

cards.text: Next, the two crops. The good seed represents the sons of the kingdom.

cards.question: In Jesus' explanation, who are the weeds?

answers.text: The sons of the evil one

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says the enemy who sowed the weeds is the devil.

cards.text: Remember, in the parable everything waits until the harvest. Now Jesus says what the harvest is, and who's doing the harvesting.

cards.question: Jesus says the harvest is the end of the ___, and the harvesters are ___.

cards.text: As the weeds are collected and burned in the fire, so will it be at the end of the age. The Son of Man will send out His angels.

cards.question: What will the Son of Man's angels weed out of His kingdom?

answers.text: Every cause of sin and all lawlessness
Every field that bore no grain

cards.text: They will throw them into the fiery furnace, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. No jokes on this card, friend. Jesus is serious here.

cards.question: After all that, what does Jesus say the righteous will do in the kingdom of their Father?

cards.text: Jesus ends with, “He who has ears, let him hear.” And He's not done teaching about the kingdom yet, friend, so keep both ears open.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 5 mentions jam, a food that isn't a cookie and isn't in the passage.

rule.text: In jokes and comparisons, cookies are the only food he mentions.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 10 quotes "I will open My mouth in parables.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "stones" is not something anyone sows, so it is a different kind of answer and is easy to rule out. "thorns" is close to "weeds", so a baker could argue that thorns sown among wheat are weeds.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the servants' question, "I bet those servants already have their sleeves rolled up, friend." and "They are READY."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The walkthrough never tells the baker that the smallest of all seeds grows into the largest of garden plants (13:32). That contrast is the point of the parable. The baker only hears that it becomes a tree and that it gets big.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: "He told them still another parable...", "Flour?", "Now you're in MY department, friend." and "I'm a cookie man, but I know dough."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Weeds, a seed, some leaven.", "BOOM, BOOM, BOOM, three parables back to back." and "Jesus spoke all these things to the crowds in parables."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup says Jesus "spoke all these things to the crowds in parables." That nearly answers card 9, which asks whether He told the crowds anything without a parable, and it rules out "True".

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card is the bare quote with no Papa Dorin voice. It also cuts the quote at "parables" so that the next choice card can ask for the rest of the line.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This card asks the baker to finish the prophet's line ("I will utter..."). That is guessing wording they haven't seen, not meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: "The Son of Man" first appears here, as the right answer, and no card ever says who He is. The baker isn't told that this is how Jesus refers to Himself.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This story card is stripped down to a bare statement ("Next, the two crops. The good seed represents the sons of the kingdom.") and has none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The right answer is an interpretation ("The sons of the evil one"), but both wrong answers are characters from inside the parable ("The owner's servants", "The hired harvesters"). This makes the right answer stand out. "Hired" is also not in the text.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: Jesus' words about the end of the age are given in Papa Dorin's own narrating voice, with no attribution to Jesus. It reads as Papa Dorin stating end-times events himself. The card also has no Papa Dorin voice.
The right answer says "all lawlessness", but 13:41 says "all who practice lawlessness". The answer changes people into an abstract idea.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This card has the same problem as card 11: Jesus' words about the fiery furnace are given in Papa Dorin's own narrating voice, with no attribution to Jesus.
"No jokes on this card, friend" refers to the app's cards, which breaks character.

rule.text: What he never talks about: the app itself, its database, its files, or how lessons are made.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the furnace line, "No jokes on this card, friend." and "Jesus is serious here."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
